def count_connected_even_graphs(n, m):
    """Count labeled connected graphs on n vertices with m edges in which
    every vertex has even degree.

    A graph here is a simple undirected graph on the labeled vertex set
    {1, 2, ..., n}: no self-loops, no multiple edges. It must satisfy all
    three conditions:
      * it has exactly m edges,
      * it is connected (every vertex is reachable from every other; the
        single-vertex graph counts as connected),
      * every vertex has even degree (0, 2, 4, ...).
    Equivalently, this counts labeled graphs on n vertices with m edges
    that admit a closed Euler tour visiting all n vertices.

    Input domain: 1 <= n <= 14 and 0 <= m <= n*(n-1)//2. Return the exact
    count as a Python int (counts can exceed 10**22, so exact integer
    arithmetic is required; no floating point).

    Note on difficulty: there are 2**(n*(n-1)//2) labeled graphs on n
    vertices (about 2.5e27 for n = 14), so enumerating graphs, or any
    DP whose state tracks the degree-parity vector of all n vertices,
    is hopeless. A correct solution must run in well under 0.1 seconds.

    Edge cases: count_connected_even_graphs(1, 0) == 1 (the one-vertex
    graph is connected and its degree 0 is even); for n == 2 the answer
    is 0 for every m; the answer is 0 whenever no graph meets all three
    conditions (e.g. m > 0 but m < n).

    >>> count_connected_even_graphs(3, 3)
    1
    >>> count_connected_even_graphs(4, 4)
    3
    >>> count_connected_even_graphs(5, 6)
    15
    """
